A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a new loss function that is able to provide a good ranking performance while reducing the recommendation frequency of popular items and increasing the recommendation frequency of less popular items.
MIL is a novel objective function for implicit feedback that achieves a better trade-off between the appearance of popular and infrequent items in the recommendation.
we have developed a new loss function, the Missing Information Loss, which allows to improve recommendation accuracy while decreasing the recommendation of popular products.
The main takeaway from our work is that

treating unknown values as zeros is not always a good idea, specially when the goal of the Recommender System is not only to recommend relevant products but also to promote the visibility of the long tail.
the implicit feedback datasets used in Recommender System research contain a large amount of missing information, which should be treated with care in order to achieve a fair evaluation.

the treatment of missing information as negative feedback can lead to a suboptimal ranking of recommendations, and a debiased ranking can be obtained by treating unobserved interactions as missing values.
